findings.reason: The protected source uses the campaign-forbidden generic local name index for the destination slot of each rigid orientation. The candidate renames only that role to orientation_slot, making the eight-way transform construction explicit without changing any coordinate rule, loop, collection, or data flow.

The inert candidate preserves the Accepted component traversal and complete dihedral canonicalization exactly while making its transform routing interview-readable. The candidate-targeted Approach also names that role and renders the coordinate families with repository-standard mathematical notation; no algorithm or asymptotic claim changes.

Global visitation extracts each four-connected island once. The eight signed coordinate permutations enumerate every quarter-turn rotation and reflected form, and subtracting coordinate minima removes translation after each transform. A rigid transformation merely permutes an island's complete family of normalized orientations, so congruent islands produce equal outer frozensets; conversely, any shared normalized orientation supplies an allowed rotation or reflection plus translation. The final set therefore has one entry per required equivalence class.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 711, Python, and the native numDistinctIslands2(grid) interface. Authenticated source evidence confirms a rectangular binary grid, four-directional connectivity, water outside all four edges, equivalence under translation, rotations of 90, 180, or 270 degrees, horizontal or vertical reflection, and an integer distinct-shape count.

The protected app source and immutable native source bound to verified submission 2065639625 use the same global traversal, relative coordinates, eight signed transforms, per-transform minimum normalization, nested frozenset identity, and final set cardinality. The candidate changes only the transform-slot local name, remains inert, and does not replace or alter the Accepted evidence.

The unchanged three authored workloads grow one dense island from 9 to 81 grid cells, forcing traversal of every cell and construction of all constant-count transforms. In a fresh real-test run, the exact candidate passed all fourteen ordinary cases and all three performance tiers with relative growth exponent -0.02 and a 1.01x largest runtime ratio; the protected source passed at +0.01 and 1.01x. A correct control that refloods and recanonicalizes the same component from every land cell passed every output but failed only performance with relative growth exponent +1.04 and a 71.85x largest runtime ratio, distinguishing linear global visitation from quadratic repeated traversal.

The candidate-targeted Approach accurately derives one-time component collection, all eight rigid orientations, translation normalization, orientation_slot routing, complete-family identity, and the bidirectional congruence argument. Its O(RC) time and O(RC) auxiliary-space claims match the candidate and branch manifest.
